questions.question: A pyramid has an equilateral triangle as its base, of which each side is 8 cm. Its slant edge is 24 cm. The whole surface area of the pyramid (in cm 2 ) is:
questions.questionHtml: A pyramid has an equilateral triangle as its base, of which each side is 8 cm. Its slant edge is 24 cm. The whole surface area of the pyramid (in cm<sup>2</sup>) is:
questions.solution:
Area of an equilateral triangle = \(\frac {\sqrt 3}{4} \times Side^2\) = \(\frac {\sqrt 3}{4} \times 8^2\) = \(16\sqrt3\) cm2

Perimeter of each triangular face of the pyramid = 24 + 24 + 8 = 56 cm

Semiperimeter of each triangular face of the pyramid  S = (A + B + C)/2 = 56/2 = 28 cm

 Area of a triangle = \(\sqrt {S(S - A)(S - B)(S - C)}\) = \(\sqrt {28(28 - 24)(28 - 24)(28 - 8)}\)= \(16\sqrt{35}\) cm2

The surface area of the pyramid ⇒ \(16\sqrt3 + 3 \times 16\sqrt{35}\) ⇒ \(\rm (16\sqrt3+48\sqrt{35})\) cm2

questions.question: If 80 litres of milk solution has 60% milk in it, then how much milk should be added to make milk 80% in the solution?
questions.questionHtml: If 80 litres of milk solution has 60% milk in it, then how much milk should be added to make milk 80% in the solution?
questions.solution:
Milk = (80 × 60/100) = 48

After adding x liters of pure milk, the total volume of the milk solution will be (80 + x) liters.

(48 + x) / (80 + x) = 0.80 ⇒ 48 + x = 0.80 × (80 + x) ⇒ 48 + x = 64 + 0.80x  ⇒ x = 80 litres

questions.question: If the highest common factor (HCF) of x and y is 15, then the HCF of 36x 2 - 81y 2 and 81x 2 - 9y 2 is divisible by ______.
questions.questionHtml: If the highest common factor (HCF) of x and y is 15, then the HCF of 36x<sup>2</sup> - 81y<sup>2</sup> and 81x<sup>2</sup> - 9y<sup>2</sup> is divisible by ______.
questions.solution:
HCF(x, y) = 15

36x2 - 81y2

⇒ 9(2 × 15p + 3 × 15q)(2 × 15p - 3 × 15q) (putting x = 15p and y = 15q) ⇒ 135 × 15 × (2p + 3q)(2p - 3q)      ....(1)

81x2 - 9y2

⇒ 9(3 × 15p + 15q)(3 × 15p - 15q) (putting x = 15p and y = 15q) ⇒ 135 × 15 × (3p + q)(3p - q)      ....(2)

From (1) and (2), we can conclude,

HCF of 36x2 - 81y2 and 81x2 - 9y2 = 135 × 15 i.e. A multiple of 135.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a square inscribed in a circle of radius 5 cm?
questions.questionHtml: What is the perimeter of a square inscribed in a circle of radius 5 cm?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Diagonal of an inscribed square = Diameter of the circle.

Diameter = 2 × Radius = 2 × 5 = 10 cm.

Perimeter of square = 2√2 × Diagonal.

Perimeter = 2√2 × 10 = 20√2 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 20√2 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the circle (r) = 5 cm

Formula Used:

Diameter of circle (d) = 2 × r

Diagonal of square (D) = Side × √2

Perimeter of square = 4 × Side

Calculations:

⇒ Diameter of the circle = 2 × 5 = 10 cm

⇒ Since the square is inscribed, its diagonal (D) = Diameter of the circle = 10 cm

⇒ Side × √2 = 10

⇒ Side = 10 ÷ √2 = 5√2 cm

⇒ Perimeter of square = 4 × 5√2

⇒ Perimeter = 20√2 cm

∴ The correct answer is 20√2 cm.

Additional Information

Area of Inscribed Square

The area of a square inscribed in a circle of radius r is given by 2r2.

Square Circumscribing a Circle

If a square circumscribes a circle, its side is equal to the diameter (2r) and its perimeter is 8r.

Diagonal Property

The diagonal of a square with side 'a' is a√2, and it is the longest distance between any two points in the square.

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a cylinder is 126 π cm 2 and its height is 14 cm, what is the volume of the cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: If the curved surface area of a cylinder is 126 π cm<sup>2</sup> and its height is 14 cm, what is the volume of the cylinder?

options.html: \(137\frac{1}{2}\) π cm3
\(128\frac{1}{2}\) π cm3
\(125\frac{1}{2}\) π cm3

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius (r) = Curved Surface Area ÷ (2 × π × height)

r = 126π ÷ (2 × π × 14) = 126 ÷ 28 = 4.5 cm

Volume of cylinder = Curved Surface Area × (r ÷ 2)

Volume = 126π × (4.5 ÷ 2) = 126π × 2.25 = 283.5π cm3

∴ The correct answer is 283½ π cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 126π cm2

Height (h) = 14 cm

Formula Used:

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × π × r × 14 = 126 × π

⇒ 28 × r = 126

⇒ r = 126 ÷ 28 = 4.5 cm

⇒ Volume = π × (4.5)2 × 14

⇒ Volume = π × 20.25 × 14

⇒ Volume = 283.5π cm3

⇒ Volume = 283½ π cm3

∴ The correct answer is 283½ π cm3.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of its volume: V = (1/3)πr2h.

Relation between Volume and CSA

For any cylinder, the ratio of its volume to its curved surface area is always r/2, simplified as V = CSA × (r/2).

questions.question: A, B, and C invested capital in the ratio of 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 8. At the end of the business term, they received the profit in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5. What is the ratio of their invested time?
questions.questionHtml: A, B, and C invested capital in the ratio of 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 8. At the end of the business term, they received the profit in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5. What is the ratio of their invested time?

options.html: 16 ∶ 18 ∶ 15

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In partnership: Profit = Capital × Time ⇒ Time = Profit ÷ Capital.

Time ratio = (2 ÷ 3) : (3 ÷ 4) : (5 ÷ 8).

LCM of denominators (3, 4, 8) = 24.

Multiply each part by 24: (2/3 × 24) : (3/4 × 24) : (5/8 × 24).

Time ratio = 16 : 18 : 15.

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 18 : 15.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of Capitals (CA : CB : CC) = 3 : 4 : 8

Ratio of Profits (PA : PB : PC) = 2 : 3 : 5

Formula Used:

Profit = Capital × Investment Time

Time = Profit ÷ Capital

Calculations:

⇒ Time of A (TA) = PA ÷ CA = 2 ÷ 3

⇒ Time of B (TB) = PB ÷ CB = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ Time of C (TC) = PC ÷ CC = 5 ÷ 8

⇒ TA : TB : TC = (2/3) : (3/4) : (5/8)

⇒ To simplify, multiply by LCM(3, 4, 8) = 24

⇒ TA = 2/3 × 24 = 16

⇒ TB = 3/4 × 24 = 18

⇒ TC = 5/8 × 24 = 15

⇒ Ratio = 16 : 18 : 15

∴ The correct answer is 16 : 18 : 15.

Additional Information

Capital Calculation

If profit ratio and time ratio are given, the ratio of capital can be found as Capital = Profit ÷ Time.

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner manages the business and may receive a fixed percentage of total profit as salary before the remaining profit is distributed.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different periods of time, the profit is shared according to the ratio of their (Capital × Time) products.

questions.question: The probabilities of solving a problem by three students A, B and C are \(\frac{3}{7},\frac{5}{9}\) and \(\frac{1}{5}\) respectively. The probability that problem will be solved is:
questions.questionHtml: The probabilities of solving a problem by three students A, B and C are \(\frac{3}{7},\frac{5}{9}\) and \(\frac{1}{5}\) respectively. The probability that problem will be solved is:
questions.solution:

P(problem is solved) = \(\frac{251}{315}\)

questions.question: Reshma covers 45 km at a speed of 15 km/h by bicycle, 80 km at a speed of 40 km/h by car, and another 6 km at a speed of 2 km/h on foot. Find her average speed for the whole journey (correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.questionHtml: Reshma covers 45 km at a speed of 15 km/h by bicycle, 80 km at a speed of 40 km/h by car, and another 6 km at a speed of 2 km/h on foot. Find her average speed for the whole journey (correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Distance = 45 + 80 + 6 = 131 km

Total Time = (45 ÷ 15) + (80 ÷ 40) + (6 ÷ 2) = 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 131 ÷ 8 = 16.375 km/h

Rounding to 2 decimal places ≈ 16.38 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 16.38 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance1 (d1) = 45 km, Speed1 (s1) = 15 km/h

Distance2 (d2) = 80 km, Speed2 (s2) = 40 km/h

Distance3 (d3) = 6 km, Speed3 (s3) = 2 km/h

Formula Used:

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = d1 + d2 + d3

⇒ Total Distance = 45 + 80 + 6 = 131 km

⇒ Time t1 = 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours

⇒ Time t2 = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time t3 = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 hours

⇒ Total Time = t1 + t2 + t3 = 3 + 2 + 3 = 8 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 131 ÷ 8

⇒ Average Speed = 16.375 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 16.38 km/h.

Additional Information

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into two equal parts with speeds x and y, then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed General Case

Average speed is always the total displacement (or total distance for scalar cases) divided by the total time taken, regardless of intermediate stops.

questions.question: A dishonest dealer marks up his goods by 50% and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1kg for 900 gm. What is his net profit percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.questionHtml: A dishonest dealer marks up his goods by 50% and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1kg for 900 gm. What is his net profit percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
Mark up by 50% and then give a 20% discount, ⇒ (1 + 0.5) × (1 - 0.2) = 1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2

Faulty balance : Actual weight is 900 gm, but reads as 1 kg

⇒ 1.2 × (1000 / 900) = 1.2 × (10 / 9) = 4 / 3

Net profit percentage = (4 / 3 - 1) × 100 = (1 / 3) × 100 = 33.33% ≈ 33%

questions.questionHtml: Find the number of diagonals of a regular polygon, sum of whose interior angles is 2700°

questions.question: The difference between the length of two parallel sides of a trapezium is 12 cm. The perpendicular distance between these two parallel sides is 60 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 1380 cm 2 , then find the length of each of the parallel sides (in cm).
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the length of two parallel sides of a trapezium is 12 cm. The perpendicular distance between these two parallel sides is 60 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 1380 cm<sup>2</sup>, then find the length of each of the parallel sides (in cm).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of parallel sides = (2 × Area) ÷ Height

⇒ Sum = (2 × 1380) ÷ 60 = 46 cm.

Given Difference = 12 cm.

Sides = (Sum ± Difference) ÷ 2 = (46 ± 12) ÷ 2 = 29 cm and 17 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 29, 17 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of trapezium = 1380 cm2

Height (h) = 60 cm

Difference between parallel sides (a − b) = 12 cm

Formula used: Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

⇒ 1380 = 1/2 × (a + b) × 60

⇒ 1380 = 30 × (a + b)

⇒ a + b = 1380 ÷ 30

⇒ a + b = 46 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ a − b = 12 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding (1) and (2): 2a = 58 ⇒ a = 29 cm

⇒ Substituting in (1): 29 + b = 46 ⇒ b = 17 cm

∴ The correct answer is 29, 17 cm.

Additional Information

Area of Trapezium

The area is calculated as the product of the average of the parallel sides and the perpendicular distance between them: Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

Median of a Trapezium

The median (mid-segment) is parallel to the bases and its length is the average of the bases: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium where the non-parallel sides are equal in length and the base angles are also equal.

questions.question: The centroid of an equilateral triangle PQR is L. If PQ = 6 cm, the length of PL is:
questions.questionHtml: The centroid of an equilateral triangle PQR is L. If PQ = 6 cm, the length of PL is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In an equilateral triangle, the distance from any vertex to the centroid (L) is equal to its circumradius (R).

Shortcut formula: PL = Side / √3

Given side PQ = 6 cm

PL = 6 / √3 = (2 × 3) / √3 = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral triangle PQR (a) = 6 cm

L is the centroid of the triangle.

Formula used:

1. Altitude (h) of an equilateral triangle = (√3 / 2) × a

2. Centroid divides the median (altitude in this case) in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex.

Calculations:

⇒ Altitude (PM) = (√3 / 2) × 6

⇒ PM = 3√3 cm

⇒ PL = (2 / 3) × PM

⇒ PL = (2 / 3) × 3√3

⇒ PL = 2√3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√3 cm.

Additional Information

Centroid of a Triangle

The point where all three medians of a triangle intersect. It divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

Equilateral Triangle Properties

For a side length a, the circumradius R = a / √3, and the inradius r = a / (2√3). The centroid, orthocenter, circumcenter, and incenter all coincide at the same point.

Area and Height

Height h = (√3 / 2) × a and Area = (√3 / 4) × a2.

questions.question: Find the exact value of cos 120°.
questions.questionHtml: Find the exact value of cos 120°.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

120° lies in the Second Quadrant (90° to 180°).

In the Second Quadrant, the Cosine function is always negative.

Reference Angle = 180° − 120° = 60°.

cos 120° = −cos 60° = −0.5.

∴ The correct answer is −0.5.

Alternate Method

Given: Angle = 120°

Formula Used: cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ

⇒ cos 120° can be written as cos(180° − 60°).

⇒ We know that cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.

⇒ cos 120° = −cos 60°.

⇒ Since cos 60° = 0.5 (or 1/2).

⇒ cos 120° = −0.5.

∴ The correct answer is −0.5.

Additional Information

ASTC Rule (Quadrant System)

All (Q-I), Silver (Q-II: Sin/Cosec), Tea (Q-III: Tan/Cot), Cups (Q-IV: Cos/Sec) identifies where functions are positive.

Standard Cosine Values

cos 0° = 1, cos 30° = √3/2, cos 45° = 1/√2, cos 60° = 0.5, cos 90° = 0.

Angle Reduction Formulas

cos(90° + θ) = −sin θ | cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ | cos(180° + θ) = −cos θ | cos(360° − θ) = cos θ.

questions.question: If 4x 2 + y 2 = 40 and xy = 6, then find the value of 2x + y.
questions.questionHtml: If 4x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 40 and xy = 6, then find the value of 2x + y.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Note the identity: (2x + y)2 = 4x2 + y2 + 4xy.

Substitute the known values 4x2 + y2 = 40 and xy = 6.

(2x + y)2 = 40 + 4 × 6 = 40 + 24 = 64.

Taking the square root on both sides: 2x + y = √64 = 8.

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method

Given:

4x2 + y2 = 40

xy = 6

Formula Used:

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

Calculations:

⇒ Consider the expression (2x + y)2.

⇒ By applying the algebraic identity, (2x + y)2 = (2x)2 + (y)2 + 2 × (2x) × (y)

⇒ (2x + y)2 = 4x2 + y2 + 4xy

⇒ Substituting the given values: (2x + y)2 = 40 + 4 × 6

⇒ (2x + y)2 = 40 + 24

⇒ (2x + y)2 = 64

⇒ 2x + y = √64

⇒ 2x + y = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8.

Additional Information

Square of a Binomial Sum

The identity (a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2 is used to relate the sum of squares and the product of two terms to the square of their sum.

Square of a Binomial Difference

The identity (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2 helps in finding the difference between terms when squares and products are known.

Difference of Two Squares

The identity a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b) is essential for factorising expressions involving the subtraction of two perfect squares.

⇒ (1/4) = (7/m) 

Solving both⇒ m = 4 × 7 ⇒ m = 28.

questions.question: Six years ago, the ratio of ages of A to B was 7 ∶ 5. After 4 years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 11 ∶ 9. What is A’s age at present?
questions.questionHtml: Six years ago, the ratio of ages of A to B was 7 ∶ 5. After 4 years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 11 ∶ 9. What is A’s age at present?
questions.solution:
A's age then = (7x + 6) + 4 = 7x + 10 and B's age then = (5x + 6) + 4 = 5x + 10

The ratio of their ages after 4 years from now will be 11:9. Thus: (7x + 10)/(5x + 10) = 11/9

questions.question: Mrs. Deepa Devi saves 30% of her salary. If she receives Rs. 42,000 per month as her salary, what is her monthly expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: Mrs. Deepa Devi saves 30% of her salary. If she receives Rs. 42,000 per month as her salary, what is her monthly expenditure?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Savings = 30% of Salary

Expenditure = (100 − 30)% = 70% of Salary

Monthly Expenditure = 70% of 42,000

Monthly Expenditure = 0.7 × 42,000 = 29,400

∴ The correct answer is ₹29,400.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Salary = ₹42,000

Savings Percentage = 30%

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Total Salary − Savings

Savings = (Savings Percentage / 100) × Total Salary

Calculations:

⇒ Savings = (30 / 100) × 42,000

⇒ Savings = 3 × 4,200 = ₹12,600

⇒ Expenditure = Total Salary − Savings

⇒ Expenditure = 42,000 − 12,600

⇒ Expenditure = ₹29,400

∴ The correct answer is ₹29,400.

Additional Information

Percentage Breakdown

Total income is always considered as 100%. If any part (like savings) is known as x%, the remaining part (expenditure) is calculated as (100 − x)%.

Ratio Method

A 30% saving implies a ratio of Savings : Expenditure = 30 : 70, which simplifies to 3 : 7. Total units (3+7) = 10, where 10 units = ₹42,000.

Percentage to Decimal

To find a percentage of a number quickly, multiply the number by its decimal equivalent (e.g., 70% = 0.70 or 70/100).

Additional Information

    • Change object into subject.
    • Change subject into object.
    • Always use the third form of the verb in the passive voice.

questions.question: How many types of writs can be issued under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India?
questions.questionHtml: How many types of writs can be issued under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3. 

Key Points

  •  Under the Constitution of India, Article 32 provides for the right to constitutional remedies, while Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs. The following are the different types of writs that can be issued under these articles:
    • Habeas corpus - to produce a person who is under illegal detention
    • Mandamus - to compel a public official or body to perform a duty
    • Prohibition - to prohibit a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction
    • Certiorari - to quash the order of a lower court or tribunal
    • Quo warranto - to question the authority or legality of a person holding a public office
  • Thus, a total of five types of writs can be issued under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India.

Additional Information

  •  Article 32 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to constitutional remedies to every citizen of India.
    • This article empowers the citizens to approach the Supreme Court of India to seek enforcement of their fundamental rights.
    • The Supreme Court has the power to issue writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto, for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.
    • The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is considered as a fundamental right in itself, and any law or action that violates the fundamental rights can be challenged under this article.
    • This article ensures that the citizens have a direct access to the Supreme Court, which is the highest court of the land, to seek justice and protection of their rights.
    • Article 32 is often regarded as the most important and valuable provision in the Indian Constitution, as it provides a powerful mechanism to protect the fundamental rights of the citizens and to ensure that the government acts in accordance with the Constitution.
  • Article 226 of the Constitution of India empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.
    • The High Court, being the highest court in a state, has wide-ranging powers to exercise judicial review over the decisions of inferior courts, tribunals, and other authorities within its territorial jurisdiction.

Uploading involves copying data from the device to the webserver, while downloading is copying files from the webserver to the device. During uploading, data travels from the user's device to the web server over the internet using protocols like HTTP or FTP.

questions.question: Which of the following Internet protocol specifies how data is exchanged over the Internet and how it should be broken into IP packets?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Internet protocol specifies how data is exchanged over the Internet and how it should be broken into IP packets?
questions.solution: TCP/IP protocol specifies data exchange and packetization on the internet. It has 4 layers: Application, Transport, Internet, and Network Access. The presentation layer is absent. OSI model has 7 layers including presentation layer. TCP/IP has fewer layers but serves the same purpose.
